question:
The degree measure of angle \(A\) is

[Figure 1](figures/1999_AMC_8_Q21_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The horizontal segment and the two lines from the bottom-left tip form a triangle whose two marked angles are known. Let \(R\) be the bottom-left tip, \(Q\) the rightmost tip, and \(P\) the intersection of the horizontal segment with the line rising from \(R\) toward the top tip. In triangle \(RPQ\), the angles at \(R\) and \(P\) are \(40^\circ\) and \(100^\circ\). Therefore,
\[
\angle PQR=180^\circ-100^\circ-40^\circ=40^\circ.
\]
Let \(X\) be the intersection marked \(110^\circ\). Since \(QA\) and \(QP\) are the same ray, and \(QX\) and \(QR\) are the same ray, the angle at \(Q\) in triangle \(AXQ\) is also \(40^\circ\). Its angle at \(X\) is the marked \(110^\circ\), so
\[
\angle A=180^\circ-110^\circ-40^\circ=30^\circ.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{30^\circ}\), choice B.
